title.narrative: Media and Information Literacy for Everyone by Everyone

description.narrative:
In critical times of climate denial, public health challenges, declining freedoms and democratic rights, all powerful digital platforms, rising hate speech, disinformation, and racism, wars and conflict, there is a vision of hope to remind people that more good is happening in the world than crises. That hope is media and inforamtion literate minds for all in critical times. Ensuring that everyone (young, older persons, men, women at all levels of society) acquire media and inforamtion literacy and digital skills contributes to strengthening peoples resilience to the ills of society often driven by disinformation and misinformation as well of abuse and misuse of digital technology and media.
UNESCO will continue to promote Media and Information Literacy (MIL) and digital competencies for all to empower citizens of all ages to adopt a critical mindset when engaging with information, digital technologies, and media. Support to Member States to develop and implement MIL policies and support its integration in formal, non-formal and informal education at all levels will be strengthened with an increased focused on digital transformation. This will be done through leading Global MIL Week celebrations and rolling-out existing UNESCO resources as well as new tools reflecting current challenges such as Hate speech and Disinformation or Generative Artificial Intelligence. UNESCO will scale up its support to youth organizations to build their capacities on MIL. Furthermore, actions will be implemented to strengthen and systemize the integration of media and information literacy in media organizations including regularities bodies.
